title: ChipBlocks behaviors manifest
description: Layer 3 of the 9-layer abstraction hierarchy (per ADR-006). Behaviors are abstract physical laws — composable rules a primitive device adopts. A resistor adopts {conducts, resists, heats}. A capacitor adopts {stores_charge, insulates}. Each behavior names a physical law + the parameters a device must provide + the symbolic equation the validator evaluates + any consequences (other behaviors implicitly triggered).

law.description: The named physical law this behavior implements.

parameters_required.description: Parameter names a device must provide when adopting this behavior. Example: 'conducts' requires ['resistance']; 'capacitance' requires ['capacitance'].

evaluates.description: Plain-text or symbolic equation the validator evaluates. Examples: 'V = I * R', 'P_heat = I^2 * R', 'Q = C * V; I = C * dV/dt'.

consequences.description: Other behavior ids implicitly triggered. E.g., 'resists' has consequences ['heats'] — a resistor that dissipates power generates heat as a follow-on physical effect.

steady_state_behavior.description: How the behavior responds in DC steady-state. E.g., 'stores_charge' has steady-state 'no DC current'; 'stores_magnetic_energy' has steady-state 'no voltage drop'.
